title: Introduce bimodal reserve holster and utilization fingerprint exporter
author: Aisha Menon
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience correlated microbursts where tenant demand alternates between short high-amplitude spikes and longer sustained waves. Existing reserve and burst controllers are tuned for one operating mode and either overspend reserved capacity or under-serve latency-sensitive tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight bimodal reserve allocator (the 'reserve holster') plus a utilization fingerprint exporter to make headroom decisions observable. Summary: 1) BimodalReserveHolster: a controller that maintains two soft reserve pools per pool-type: a short-window fast-reserve for microbursts (sub-second to 30s) and a sustained-reserve for longer waves (1m-30m). The holster uses probabilistic allocation to allow opportunistic usage by lower-priority tenants while preserving SLO-backed guaranteed headroom for higher tiers. 2) UtilizationFingerprintExporter: samples per-pool utilization histograms, burst-rate transitions, and allocation decisions into a compact fingerprint vector emitted every 15s. Fingerprints are exposed as Prometheus metrics and JSON blobs to the telemetry pipeline for downstream anomaly detection and trend correlation. Design highlights: - Configurable thresholds: fastReservePct, sustainedReservePct, decayTauSeconds, allocationSkewCap - Admission policy: fastReserve is preemptible; sustainedReserve prefers non-preemptible allocations for guaranteed throughput. - Overflow behavior: when both reserves are exhausted, requests fall back to soft-degrade handler with prioritized shedding and warm-pool fast-paths. - Safety: conservative default configs preserve current behavior (no change to SLOs out of the box). Backwards compatibility: controller registers behind a feature flag "bimodal_reserve_holster" (off by default). When disabled, scheduler/reservation behavior is unchanged. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy holster in read-only telemetry mode to gather fingerprints (2 weeks) 2) Enable fast-reserve only in canary clusters with 10% traffic (1 week) 3) Enable sustained-reserve with gradual knob increases per region (2–4 weeks) 4) Monitor fingerprint drift and cost delta, revert if P99 latency increases > 5% or cost rises > 7% relative to baseline. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of controller and allocation algorithm - [x] Fingerprint exporter and Prometheus metrics - [x] Unit tests for allocation invariants and overflow behavior - [x] Integration harness in benchmark-lab - [x] Runbook entry and rollout gating - [x] Feature flag gating and CLI toggles Observability and telemetry: new metrics prefixed resholster_* and fingerprint_*; labels: pool, region, tenant_tier, window. The fingerprint JSON includes: timestamp, pool_id, fast_util_p50/p90/p99, sustained_util_p50/p90/p99, burst_transition_rate, allocated_fast, allocated_sustained, opportunistic_util. Tests and validation: - Local unit tests covering probabilistic allocation and decay - E2E in benchmark-lab using synthetic microburst traces (attached harness config) - Canary run: sample traces show reduced P50 tail for tiered tenants and stable sustained throughput for long waves Documentation: added operator notes to dedicated/README and a short HOWTO in console runbooks describing knobs and interpretation of fingerprint vectors. Related: Linear ENG-4829 (bimodal headroom exploration), ENG-7132 (tenant-priority admission).

b2f4d1a: add UtilizationFingerprintExporter and Prometheus hooks
c7e2b9d: config defaults, feature-flag wiring and CLI toggles
d4f5a0b: unit tests for allocation logic and overflow behaviour
e1a7c3f: integration harness and benchmark-lab scenario
f0b1d2e: docs: operator notes and runbook sample
release_notes: Introduce a feature-flagged bimodal reserve allocator for dedicated fleets and a compact utilization fingerprint exporter for improved anomaly detection and headroom analysis. Disabled by default; operators should follow the documented rollout plan.
review_comments: Riley Chen: Nice isolation between fast and sustained reserves. Please add a short note about expected memory overhead of the fingerprint exporter (how many labels and series).
Aisha Menon: Added prom series estimate in comments and lowered default fingerprint cardinality by aggregating on pool_id+tier. See benchmark-lab results included in commits.
Priya Kapoor: Can we ensure the fastReservePct default matches current microburst protection for GA tenants? Otherwise tiered performance might regress.
Aisha Menon: Set fastReservePct default to 12% for GA tenants to match historical headroom observed in production traces. Documented in holster_defaults.yaml.
Ethan Sussman (approved): Verified unit tests and ran canary against benchmark-lab. Fingerprint vectors look stable. Approving for merge behind flag.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals. Feature gated and disabled by default. Canary run scheduled per rollout plan; ops runbook added and alerts wired to paging for quick rollback conditions.
notes_for_ops: Operators: enable feature via rdctl feature enable bimodal_reserve_holster --clusters <canary>. Observe fingerprint drift dashboard (dash/fingerprint-drift). If P99 latency > 5% or cost > 7% vs baseline, disable flag and trigger rollback runbook: ops/rollback-bimodal.md.
risk_assessment: Medium: algorithmic allocation is conservative by default but changes headroom accounting. Mitigation: feature flag, read-only telemetry phase, canary rollout, and explicit cost/latency gates.
